text:
Notice curled against the freezer, soy sauce ringing half the door,
magnet weak enough to lose it every time the box fan sweeps the floor.
Seventh lands on Thursday, lease in ballpoint: money order, cash, or trace,
stairwell radiator knocking like a second hand that learned the pace.
Friday's doubles folded in a sock I tucked behind the dryer vent,
still a hundred light on water if the insert wasn't what they meant.
Mrs. Chen don't knock on 4B, envelope, a slipper, then she goes,
hallway keeps her scrape a second, then the scrape is finished, door is closed.
Quarter jar, two tens, a five, the bus pass lying face-down flat,
fare stays with me through the morning so the jar can answer, not go slack.
Super's digits penciled on the jamb, he answers somewhere on the third,
game show under coughing, both arriving half a second after heard.
Partial if the Friday holds, he tells me, turning down the stair,
keys drag on the railing, laugh track pacing him along the repair.
Tape the yellow level, smooth the curl, my mother doesn't need the date,
alarm for five a.m., before the office lets the deadbolt learn it's late.

Badge clock takes my thumb at 10:58 and coughs a tired green,
dock lights answer in a flat hum, numbness climbing up the seam.
Pallet jack complains at bay fourteen, the patch they poured in May,
I know the pitch, I do not look, the sound already named the bay.
Coffee from the steel machine still tastes like filter more than bean,
heat is what I paid for, heat against the wrist the glove left mean.
Preacher on the radio past two, he's selling rest by the bag,
shrink-wrap flashes count the sermon, let the promise miss me while it drags.
Break room digits blinking zeros, no one bothers to reset,
sandwich sweating through the foil on a chair the rivet left upset.
Delgado lifts two fingers, doesn't slow the mast to wave,
backup beeper is the greeting, I reverse out of the way.
Four o'clock, a crack of panel lets a dirty morning through,
birds take over on the asphalt, loud and punctual as a crew.
Punch-out leaves a 6:02 in red I don't stay long enough to read,
sun gets in the driver's seat before I do, and takes the lead.

Cleats still caked along the tub although I told him rinse them twice,
I work the clay out with a brush so Coach won't call the mud a price.
Algebra face-down on the counter, number four is where he quit,
pencil light enough to lift, I finish what he wouldn't admit.
Mom left rice and underlined the order: in the house by ten,
phone lights names I wouldn't offer chairs to if they reached the den.
Nine-forty, Dixon's lawn, his hood against the neighbor's light,
seven minutes saved on foot, and something smaller lost tonight.
Practice ran long, that's the version, but the knuckles write their own,
I read the scuff before the sentence, let the sentence stand alone.
Rice and hot sauce, chicken didn't stretch, we split the little that it did,
he says a scout was in the bleachers, I say show me what you hid.
Charger goes inside the drawer so sleep arrives before the scrolls,
clean shirt on the chair back, collar open where his hand already knows.
Second deadbolt sounds like doubt if you are listing how he moves,
I count his breathing through the drywall till the bus sighs and the block approves.

Steam writes on the glass the way her palm did, winter ninety-eight,
print is gone, the cloud still comes, it keeps the same appointment late.
Onions hit the oil and travel halfway down the hall before
the neighbor's dog begins a comment, then remembers to ignore.
Shaker lid is tape and toothpick, salt decided by the hand,
bay leaf turning in the simmer like a boat that never asked to land.
Cast iron older than my license, seasoned past the factory shine,
she refuses any skillet that would break the old design.
Peels drop where her finger points, the potato eyes go in the bin,
she hums a bar, abandons it, and doesn't pick it up again.
Matchbook shimmed beneath the short leg keeps the bowls from rocking loose,
we eat above the drawer where due-dates used to sleep in rubber loops.
Extra portion, no announcement, just a ladle and a glance,
I clear the plate down to the pattern so the quiet can't call it chance.
Yellow soap stretched one more evening, foam collapsing into lace,
burner ticks, then loses interest, lets the kitchen keep its place.

Box tab soft at fourteen-A, the cardboard giving at the thumbs,
sedan the photo caught is gray the way a rainy afternoon becomes.
Witness wrote around then, pen skipping on the downstroke,
detective circled till the paper at the circle almost broke.
Left shoe partial, plaster missing at the outer heel,
nephew named the tread with certainty, then took it back by feel.
Signature thins out to doubt, the last name tapering to less,
coffee oval on the margin ate the digits off the address.
Laundromat changed owners, changed the neon, dryers stayed the same,
vent still breathes into the alley like the alley kept the name.
Sister calls on the date we don't say out loud anymore,
I tell her who still answers, not the porches that ignore.
Most of it is copies of a single afternoon that stalled,
bus route gone since oh-nine, jacket brown, no label to recall.
She said brown once, not maroon, we kept the garment for that thread,
cold is other people buttoning their other coats instead.

Folder thick with copies, every copy carrying a stamp,
pay stubs pale where toner missed the hours underneath the lamp.
Lease from nineteen, cosigner reduced to one decisive line,
not a name I set a plate for, just a name that rented time.
W-2s arranged by year until they look like they agree,
statements: rent, then nothing moving, then the overdraft and fee.
Carbon title, Civic gone, the buyer met us in a lot,
mileage hurried, sixes drooping toward a four the way the pen forgot.
Itemized in codes I matched to English after work,
carrier approved the big one, left the little ones to lurk.
Stranger-ready pages wear a yellow tab along the side,
binder clips bit down where paper clips got tired and opened wide.
Every page can place me in a room the lease will not repeat,
dates line up like alibis for cash that left without a receipt.
If the window asks for where I was, I slide the folder, not a speech,
dull survives a cross-exam, and dull is harder to impeach.

Time clock shaves the minute if I punch inside the four,
so I wait beside the cage until the digit frees the door.
Last tote tilted on the roller, label lifting at the seam,
supervisor taps the board and never says the word we mean.
Dry-erase receives my name in strokes much thinner than the last,
Wednesday's column full of ghosts of Wednesdays that already passed.
Case-three height is muscle memory, the eyes just tag along,
poster keeps a neutral spine, the poster never proved it strong.
Break I skipped still sits inside a sentence no one read aloud,
I buy hummus I don't finish, just to stand where standing's allowed.
Amber lamps give up in order, lot becomes a darker park,
engine ticking down to metal, granola cracking in the dark.
Seat reclined a single notch, the seek keeps walking up the band,
nothing sticks, I let it travel, company that doesn't want a hand.
Counting greens on Airport Road, each one a minute I reclaim,
from the version of the evening that the time clock took and renamed.

He still knocks, two taps and a wait, although the mailbox has his name,
toothbrush in the cup beside her blue one, handle turned the same.
I slide his boots an inch off perfect just to keep the mat my fact,
then I slide them back, annoyed at owning such a petty act.
Hinge that scraped my childhood mornings hasn't scraped since he took pains,
dinner came and went without it, silence where it used to complain.
Sunday speaker, his other son, they split a game down play by play,
I wash the bowl and learn the kid's week so I know the father's way.
No speeches, just the question, did a red envelope arrive,
I say no, he nods like no is news he's glad to keep alive.
Snow made rumors of the bus stops, so he nodded at the seat,
heater on high, the quiet doing more than any speech.
Trestle shortcut, taken plainly, no lesson grafted to the turn,
dropped me where the awning kept the punch clock out of weather's concern.
First name only, rule I wrote and didn't hang above the hook,
locking what he quieted still answers, even without a look.

The nine retires its route sign, letters folding into dark,
driver knows my face from transfers, lets me pass without remark.
Vent blows wet wool, nickel, fryer, night's familiar little blend,
laundromat in sliding panes, one red still tumbling at the end.
Seats are warm from Grant Street bodies that got off and didn't stay,
I take the cushion that still holds, and brace the bag so it won't sway.
Route screen looping one polite instruction it can't complete,
quarry stretch with lamps gone missing, yellow paint beneath our feet.
Earbud snare two rows ahead, the owner sleeping through the leak,
temple on the glass conducting every seam the road can speak.
I step off one stop early so the brakes don't have to learn my gate,
chime is small, the driver answers out of habit, not debate.
Bag against the hip that did the lifting, frost along the walk,
porch light startles when I reach it, like a watchman woken up to talk.
Key fights back because the cold got in the barrel of the lock,
tail lights shrink, the street resumes the quiet job of being blocked.

The charge light blinks against the sock, a green I do not get to spend,
strap still warm, the plastic smelling faintly like a floorboard vent.
Curfew is a circle, legal right up to the maple's root,
past it, every step is paperwork that nobody will prosecute.
Laundromat a block too far, I measured it against the sheet,
so the bathroom sink does shirts, and drips all night above my feet.
They text a pin across the river, tell me not to be uptight,
I send the no before it softens, stay inside the charger light.
Shower takes a grocery bag, a band, a cuff held out of spray,
I hate the steps, I hate them less than one more speech about the delay.
I eat standing at the window, legal sidewalk in the frame,
maple just beyond the glass, dividing ordinance from name.
Sleep turned so the housing doesn't press the spot it likes to crown,
dreams cross Maple like it's nothing, leave the crossing on the ground.
Same three questions, coffee scorched, the clipboard warmer than the talk,
I show the green, he nods at it, and neither of us extends the walk.

Perforated, my name typed, the ink still easy to smear,
cupped in both hands on the bus, which tells the aisle more than it should hear.
Friday rope against my wrist, I mouth the total till it's flat,
teller counts it twice, then bands it, face confirming only that.
Second line is smaller, deductions sitting where the hours should have been,
I get it, getting it does not return the difference again.
Oil for the ticking fan belt, loaf, the script in generic white,
bus pass funded through the seventh, nothing new to catch the light.
He taps the box we always passed, the one above the price we pay,
two bowls, a finger to my lips, the brag can wait outside the day.
Mom finds the stub beneath the shutoff notice, doesn't dress it as pride,
files it in the jar of papers that did what they were printed to decide.
Rubber band still grooved into my wrist where all those hours went,
I rinse the groove out at the kitchen tap and watch the dent relent.
Darius said enjoy it, grinning at the locker like a dare,
I enjoyed the oil light dying, left the grinning hanging there.

Hallway buzz lives in my filling, fluorescent never quite at rest,
bolted chairs, split vinyl, magazines about a coast we will not test.
Vending slot debates the dollar, then agrees and drops the weight
of pretzels no one asked for, salt to occupy the hands that wait.
Squeak we want and squeak that passes, we can sort them in the tile,
passing squeak, the shoulders lower, wanted squeak, we counterfeit a smile.
Mother's ring against the armrest counting numbers she won't say,
Father stands so sitting doesn't look like he agreed to stay.
Wheels go by behind a curtain, voices leveled into calm,
we watch the floor's gray speckle so we don't supply the harm.
Cart coffee, brown by courtesy, the paper thinning at the grip,
I hold it till the heat becomes a story I can sip.
Muted set, a stranger winning money in a room we cannot hear,
captions landing half a breath behind, no laugh track landing here.
Doctor's sentence shorter than the hallway he consumed to arrive,
we nod as if the nod could shelve it, nod again to keep it alive.

The bell is bright and out of touch with anybody coming through,
rings asleep in felt, guitar necks, trumpet dull, the felt gone blue.
Index card, the serial, he matches it against the plate,
battery at one bar, dent along the grip I know by weight.
He names a figure, lets it sit between us like a third man's name,
I say yes, because the rent is ruder than a little shame.
He sees the date scratched in the base, no question, no delay,
foam receives it like a habit, careful work, then looks away.
Purple carbon stains the thumbnail, thirty nights are on the slip,
camera sleeps beneath the counter, label out, along the strip.
Laptop holding all the pictures is a whim away from dead,
I tell the sidewalk they are copied, which revises what I said.
Bus seat, shoulder strangely lighter, cash a narrow sort of gain,
ticket slipped inside the paperback so wash day doesn't take the claim.
Twenties counted face-up, no flourish, nothing added for the dent,
bell re-rings me into weather, cheerful, like it knew what the money meant.

Short curtains, so the midnight bus stop sees the microwave's green clock,
glass on Foster, glass on Tenth, a corner with nowhere to block.
Tuesday's argument still living in the gesture of a glass,
someone at the stop reenacts it with their eyebrows as they pass.
Dying plant pulled back from Foster so the brown won't be a show,
still it leans toward the window like the window is a place to go.
Television paints the ceiling, and the ceiling paints the street,
strangers get the color changes, miss the sentence underneath.
I change my shirt inside the closet though the closet door won't latch,
privacy becomes a closet when the walls refuse to catch.
Landlord calls the glass a feature, writes it in the listing's glow,
feature means the curtains cost me, feature means the block will know.
Dinner happens under window-line, the bowls down by our feet,
laughter waits until the bus pulls off and takes its audience up the street.
Morning, I rotate the plant so something green still faces in,
silhouettes can have the sidewalk, faces stay behind the thin.

The letter says we must decline in language soft as office air,
five four one is printed bold, as if the bold was always fair.
Phone bill from a winter I was twenty, still alive inside the machine,
then the clinic, then a card I cosigned, then the long gap in between.
Forty-dollar application, stamped before the answer came,
thank-you paragraph, then silence where a set of keys would have a name.
I call the bureau, wait on hold beside a trumpet no one chose,
agent reads the items back, each one a door I thought I'd closed.
Secured card in a drawer, two hundred of my own to borrow mine,
pay it monthly, watch the needle, hope the needle learns a line.
Grocery still runs on debit, debit only asks the balance, not the lore,
Tuesday either has the money, or the card is plastic, nothing more.
He says the winter bill can move if all the paperwork is clean,
I copy dates and certify the packet, mail it, keep the green.
Receipt is thin and green and proof the argument has left my care,
somewhere a stranger reads December, and decides if it was fair.

Program thin as onion skin, two-fourteen circled, Wanda's pen,
cardboard fan says Lane and Sons, and stirs the heat around again.
Grandma's peppermint, the kind that cracks, she slips it without a look,
sermon rolling, I take notes that aren't the notes she thinks I took.
Car wash on the sheet for Saturday, the youth are short, it starts at eight,
nephew's scholarship gets mentioned, amens land a little late, but straight.
I sit the back where standing doesn't single anyone for show,
grandma stands, I stand beside her, fan still moving, words still slow.
Bills that lived past oil and cereal, folded till they almost hide,
basket doesn't slow or speed up, doesn't weigh, and doesn't decide.
Fellowship is starch and sugar, coffee that could sand a board,
I wash the tall pots afterward, the steam a quieter reward.
Foil on two plates, she slides them, says the second isn't mine to hold,
someone's week ran long and heavy, carry both and leave the story told.
Fan still in my fist outside, the cardboard warped from all that air,
dashboard holds it facing forward, name still readable in the glare.

Bell sticks on the upswing, Adeyemi palms the frame and lets it go,
cooler needs a shoulder, and the regulars already know.
Notebook by the register, the tabs in pencil, names and sums,
nobody announces paying, Friday is a page that comes.
Kid spills coins across the mat and stacks them into shaky piles,
Adeyemi helps him stack, the juice can wait, the line can wait a while.
Lotto slips in plastic hooks, the same three numbers every week,
he sells the hope, he also sells the milk, and doesn't blur the receipt.
Cat asleep on rice, they call him Dollar, which is not a joke they force,
he ignores the bell, the coins, the jokes, and answers only one man's course.
Dome went dark in May and stayed, he says replacement isn't in the quote,
people still adjust their hands beneath it, habit older than the note.
After ten, the cooler darkens, street inherits all the noise,
one bulb, bolt shot softly, nothing staged, and no goodbyes.
Two weeks off the notebook, pencil ticking, neither of us makes a speech,
torn bag of plantain chips, he calls it damaged, sends it toward the street.

Contacts with no last names, just a role: dentist-new, and job, the night,
scrolling is a kind of census, half the doors are out of light.
Landline for a kitchen that got sold and painted over twice,
once a year I let it ring, and nobody picks up to give advice.
Number for a counter where the slices used to come out fast,
now a robot books a clinic, same ten digits, different past.
Thumb still draws her number in the dark, a shape it learned by heart,
I stop one key before the send, a small correction, private art.
Foreman Roy, the trailer number, digits ending four four two,
trailer gone, the lot is gravel, Roy still answers, coughs, says who.
One I blocked, then unblocked, from a month I will not advertise,
left it in the list, deleting would have sounded like disguise.
Mom says don't erase the dead ones, says the phone is not a grave,
I leave them lower in the list, where a tired thumb won't misbehave.
Codes I carried out of towns I do not visit anymore,
thumb still walks those hallways, even if the hallway has no door.

The icing says Nya, purple border, seven candles leaning east,
she shrugs, corrects a candle, says the cake can learn her name at least.
Polo has a purple thumbprint, warehouse logo half erased,
she finds it, laughs, the gap-tooth whistle riding in the trace.
Gift is skates, the helmet with the shop-stickers on the shell,
off, then on, then off again, she edits stickers, knows them well.
No bounce house, that was last year, this year sprinkler, grass, and plates,
speaker in the window, one song skipping where the chorus waits.
Rosa took the final hour, I will take her Thursday on the floor,
Nia sees the match, not Rosa, sees the flame, and not the chore.
Singing starts in three keys, nobody apologizes for the pitch,
smoke climbs, wish stays with her, I don't fish for it or snitch.
She sleeps with one skate in the bed, the other on the rug, still laced,
helmet on the dresser, stickers arguing, the day still on her face.
I scrape the wrong name off the cardboard, save a square for her to find,
purple on the thumb at midnight, Thursday already in my mind.

Radio low, blue drawstring biting where I grip it on my knee,
Dana says the dog, the bedtime, bus stop, never says the bag to me.
Lemon smell, the carpet damp, the windows cracked to let it dry,
top bunk's mine, the bottom slat says Marcus in a marker, thick and high.
Magnet letters on the fridge, the rules are short, the letters small,
shoes off at the mat, I leave mine on, then off, then on, then stall.
Mango sniffs the drawstring, sneezes, tail decides before the talk,
leans on my shin for one quick second, like he doesn't need a walk.
Dana's number on a sticky, circled twice, she taps it, then she goes,
house gets quiet in the way that asks, I answer by unpacking slow.
Shirt goes in their washer so the other house's smell will finally quit,
left side of the drawer, not more, the right stays Marcus, I make it fit.
Shoes beside the mat, second try, I point them like I mean to stay,
night light in the hall, not babyish, I leave it on, and leave it that way.
Nobody asks about the other house, the cereal just hits the bowl,
tape on the lunch, my name spelled right, I read it twice, then read it whole.

Four-ten, pants on the chair, they kept the shape of yesterday's bend,
radiator shirt, warm at the shoulder, cuffs still cold where night won't end.
Key, then waiting, breath in front of me, the belt complains, then turns,
coffee in a jar, too sweet, the sweet is what the dark part earns.
Radio discusses weather for a coast I will not see,
black ice in the seam of my ramp is the warning meant for me.
Floodlight, two cars, mine and Rosa's, frost along the wiper line,
finger lifted off her wheel, the whole good morning, small and fine.
Batter side today, not bleach, the hands clock in before the mind,
second tray, I finally wake, the waking running late behind.
Break is standing in the cold so cold can feel like another room,
steam off coffee, stars still out, the stars don't have to answer soon.
No proverb in it, just the order: ramp, then jar, then sticking key,
floodlight, Rosa's finger, batter, second tray, the dark, and me.
Yesterday is in the coat already, folded at the seam,
zipper follows, no announcement, morning doesn't ask a theme.

Sign pole with no sign, the bolts still rusting in a face,
weeds write through the asphalt, spelling nothing, taking space.
Food King's letters peeled, the blue they left is paler than the sky,
one cart in the corral, upright, as if the upright still applies.
Posted notice gone to fiber, kids cut through along the seam,
grass wore down to packed dirt, brighter, saying fence is just a screen.
Floodlight burning for a bill that nobody is left to claim,
moths keep faith with it regardless, circling the same small flame.
I used this aisle when aisle was real, the cart meant milk and heat and bread,
now the aisle is weather, white lines fading under what the weeds have spread.
A couch faces the avenue, the foam split open by the rain,
sitting is a thing it did in someone's room, it will not sit again.
Footprint where the shade was, gravel cleaner than the rest around,
squint, it's walls, then stop the squint, and let the present have the ground.
Parked the way I used to park, nose pointed where the doors would be,
nothing in a bag, no list, the floodlight doesn't question me.

No hazards on, no show for no one, cabin ticking while it cools,
hands at ten and two, not folded, folding felt like someone else's rules.
Alternator first, it clicks, the click is not a metaphor I need,
Keisha's rent is second, due on Friday, short, I say the shortfall, not a creed.
Skip the language that makes trouble sound like product on a shelf,
dollar amount, abscess, Friday, Keisha's voice, the facts themselves.
Fog, I draw a square, the plant door shows up, ordinary, gray,
nothing speaks inside the square, the door is just the door today.
If a count exists, then count the click, the Friday gap, the gum,
I can work the shift, I know the motions, I can't make the three a sum.
Amen feels too much like closing, so I don't, I let it hang,
wipers once, the square smears, I redraw it with the side of my hand.
Marisol knocks the glass two times, the way she does when time is thin,
I nod, the nod is true, the rest can ride the visor, folded in.
Transmission stays unspoken, naming it would park it in the day,
zipper up, the nod already given, prayer left open, not put away.

Eighty even, chat named Upstairs, message said the room, said cash,
photo shows a bar rail, limes cut, cousin grinning, raised a glass.
I keep the screenshot for the timestamp, not to build a scene,
sensitive, they call it, timestamp doesn't care what I mean.
Deon slides a text outside the thread, all worry, all surprise,
same Deon in the photo, wristband, lime, the flash still in his eyes.
I don't do a speech in Upstairs, speeches are a kind of mask,
I ask for forty back by Friday, plain, and leave the larger ask.
Andre writes a paragraph on loyalty, the paragraph is cheap,
loyalty that photographs itself at midnights it can't keep.
Tape along the window crack, the landlord's note still taped in blue,
eighty was the gap exactly, eighty spent itself past due.
I mute it, not a manifesto, just so names don't hit my screen at night,
problems do not need a group chat, they were doing fine without the light.
Mom asks why the jar is light, I say the room, which is and isn't true,
both halves accurate, the hard part is the half I let the chat undo.

Apron riding shotgun, name tag ticking every time I brake,
fourteen minutes on the clock to cross the river, change, and not be late.
Station bathroom, lock half-hearted, I swap shirts above the sink,
collar still announcing fryer, bleach will edit it, but not the ink.
Diner tag gets pocketed so clinic fluorescent doesn't see,
clinic badge is on a reel, it taps my chest, a second me.
Both apps think they own the spine, the feet, the evening, and the night,
I let them think it, thinking pays, the truth is fourteen, tight.
Cook says I'm flying, slides a sandwich I don't have the minutes to eat,
four bites in the car, the river, red light, crumbs across the seat.
Grocery bag of clinic shoes, the diner pair still damp with spill,
red light, dome light, swap, a private pit stop, looking more like skill.
Pell can smell the afternoon and chooses not to make it talk,
chin toward the locker, I start lining trays, the diner in my walk.
Sleep's a rumor scheduled somewhere after one, if one arrives,
four-ten loaded in the phone, the gap between the clocks survives.

Coasters aren't optional, the wood remembers every cup that failed,
I use one, she still slides it closer, care that looks like being detailed.
Dish of butterscotch, the good glass, company that rarely came,
I unwrap one, she watches sideways, counting without saying the name.
Man on the piano, smile I inherited as story, not as face,
she dusts the frame the way she dusts the others, ordinary grace.
Greens in the pot, Bengay uncapped, the hallway negotiates the two,
clock chimes early by an hour, she says let it, she already knew.
Remote inside a plastic sleeve so buttons don't go soft with thumbs,
game shows, choir, a newsman she corrects, correction is the thing that comes.
Mother's old room, trophies on a shelf, the gold gone brassy, names not mine,
I don't rotate them, don't align them, let the dust be her design.
Containers nested, labeled, rice enough to feed the extra chair,
she doesn't have an extra eater, extra is the care she doesn't declare.
Motion light is late, I clear my throat, the bulb considers, then it throws,
she was at the door already, hearing has a head start on the glow.

Jacket borrowed, Ellis's shoulders, cuffs a little past the bone,
silver pins along the seam he set while talking on the phone.
Tag still tucked beneath the arm, the scissors lost to rushing out,
it scratches May's hug, petty, sharp, a thing I didn't mean to bring about.
His tie, my knot, the knot unequal, leaning like a bad intent,
no one is scoring silk, they're counting chairs, and who the chairs meant.
Printed solemn, four neat blocks, a version pressed and clean and grand,
driveway grease and carburetor laughter didn't make the program's plan.
Someone at the repast asks me if I am Ellis, seeing cloth,
I tell her no, the jacket's his, she nods, the mix-up gentle, soft.
Night, I hang it how he asked, the shoulders back on his own door,
tag cut out at last, the scratch is over, pins still keeping score.
Shoes are mine and they betray me, squeaking where the room is still,
I step when other people step, and hide inside the larger will.
Flower in the buttonhole, I couldn't name it, warm before the noon,
droops in honesty, I let it, not everything should look in tune.

Delta crack above the fixture, pale against the older paint,
I name the branches in a whisper, naming just to not feel faint.
Fridge clocked in, a small employment, buzzing like it means to stay,
then it clocks back out, and quiet takes the overtime without a say.
Neighbor's set: a laugh, a shot, a softer sound that might be tears,
I get the sequence, not the names, the sequence is enough for years.
Phone face-down, I know the glow would make the list a little loud,
so it stays there, warm, face-hidden, like a mouth I won't allow.
Amber stain along the delta, maybe roof, maybe a pipe,
I invent its borders, countries, just to give the hour a type.
Tomorrow's list is belt, then call, then form, then bus, then eight,
saying it in order doesn't do it, order is a kind of bait.
Siren slides toward the east side, I hold still to hear it turn,
it fades, the fade is kindness, I give the ceiling back its burn.
Sleep arrives the way a bus arrives, indifferent, a little late,
I don't thank it, I just board it, leave the delta with its weight.

Books go in a bin because the good crate split along the spine,
his mug stays on the hook, the chip faced out, the chip was never mine.
Photo booth strip on the freezer, both of us with cheaper hair,
I leave it curled at one corner, he can choose the keeping, I was there.
Key centered on the counter, note would be a second, smaller lease,
plant stays, it won't survive the back seat, he inherits dirt and peace.
Stain beside the heater, wine or something, we stopped calling it by name,
deposit already spent in our heads, the forfeit older than the blame.
Super checks the smoke alarm, the latches, outlets, with a look,
I initial on the line he taps, and set his pen back on the hook.
Their fridge hum, I won't hear it after midnight, new one's got a knock,
one more second in the doorway, then I pull the door and lock.
Lamar's truck, drywall dust, he says the mattress is a puzzle, not a fight,
diagonal, then groan, then in, the groan is ours, the win is slight.
Lower on the springs, he asks me once if I am good, then lets it be,
mirror keeps the mattress, crate and bin, the mug stays out of frame, still free.

Nothing had a draft, the window didn't seat, the streetlight did the lamp,
mattress from a cousin, on the floor, no frame, the floor became the camp.
One bent pot, the handle ticks, whatever dinner is has got to fit,
spoon came with the noodles, plastic, softens, I eat slow so it won't split.
Dead outlet, so the cord escapes the room and borrows from the hall,
Friday is the word he offered, not a date that I can call.
Door slab on two crates, that's the table, measure of a meal, a form,
it wobbles, paper folded under, paper is the first repair I perform.
No curtain, so the streetlight draws a hard stripe over pot and bed,
I sleep on the unlit side, and let the lit side be the street instead.
Morning count is pot and spoon and mattress, cord, the door we called a board,
add a washed cup, drying upside down, the first thing here I didn't borrow.
I don't send a picture, pictures want a caption and a climb,
the room is draft and stripe and one clean cup, and that is plenty, this time.
Boots beside the dead outlet, pointing where the shift will start,
nothing shifted just enough to give the boots a place, a part.
